newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas eases on storage draws, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas eases on storage draws, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mostly softer Wednesday as many buyers turned to storage supplies and milder weather was forecast to arrive in the Midwest this weekend, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast gas traded in the high-$2.60s to low-$2.70s, with the higher-priced deals evident shortly before nomination deadlines.
As the below-normal temperatures lingered in the Midwest and Northeast, buyers were withdrawing gas from storage instead of entering the spot market to meet the heating demand, traders said.
In the Midcontinent, where buyers were also tapping into storage inventories, prices slipped about five to six cents to the high-$2.50s.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to be only slightly below-normal by Saturday and then moderate further into next week.
In west Texas, Permian prices fell by about five cents to the high-$2.40s to low-$2.50s, while at the southern California border gas sold in the mid-to-high $2.60s.
On the opposite coast, New York city-gate prices continued to strengthen as traders reported closing deals in the $3.50-3.60 range, up another five to 15 cents from Tuesday's levels.
Separately, Rochester Gas and Electric Corp's 470 megawatt Ginna nuclear power plant has returned to service after shutting down on Oct 24 for repairs, Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.
